page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the E2 family, designed for compute-heavy workloads. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance primarily in the average tier for multi-threaded operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2680.97, while multi-core performance falls in the middle 50% at 21496.93. Memory bandwidth is stable, with cached small-block reads reaching 645.66 GB/sec and uncached large-block writes at 35.27 GB/sec. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show poor performance, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-16 offers a resource density optimized for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. This makes it a practical option for workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving, where its average multi-core capabilities and Redis performance of 15.91 million operations per second can be leveraged without paying for idle memory. It is also appropriate for lightweight LLM inference, achieving 904.78 tokens per second for prompt processing on small 135M models.
